title: Givfunds: Social Media Storytelling for Financial Inclusion | Studio 1947
description: How Studio 1947 turned Givfunds' grassroots financial literacy work into Exemplar Award and awareness posters, made to be shared as a badge of honour.
ogDescription: Exemplar Award posters and awareness statistics that made Givfunds' financial literacy mission shareable.

hero.alt: The givfunds logo: a white lowercase wordmark with an infinity mark over the g and v, underlined, on brand red

body: Givfunds (givfunds.org) works at the ground level of financial inclusion in India. It funds the educators, community organisers and everyday changemakers who close the gap a spreadsheet of statistics never quite closes on its own.

This is one of Studio 1947's oldest working relationships. The design work began with our founder, Rabi, before Studio 1947 existed as a studio. What follows is part of that ongoing collaboration: a running social media system built one poster at a time.

sections.heading: The Brief: Two Kinds of Post, One Voice

sections.label: The Challenge
body: Givfunds needed its feed to do two different jobs without reading as two different accounts. Honour the people doing the work of financial inclusion on the ground. And make the scale of the problem land in a single glance: a country where three in four adults aren't financially literate.
Recognition and statistics are opposite moods. One is warm and personal, the other is blunt and numeric. The brief was to hold both inside one red-and-white identity.

cards.title: Recognition, Not a Certificate
cards.body: Exemplar Award posters built to feel like a share-worthy honour, not an official document nobody reposts.

cards.title: Statistics With a Sting
cards.body: National-scale numbers on financial literacy, redrawn so the headline figure is the first and only thing you read.

cards.title: One Identity, One Red
cards.body: Every post, portrait or pure typography, carries the same givfunds red, wordmark and globe-and-link header.

sections.heading: The Exemplar Awards
sections.label: Recognition Posters
body: Two of the people Givfunds' work touches: Varsha Patil, honoured for changing classrooms one student at a time, and Alamelu V, honoured for rebuilding her community's resilience after it broke. Each portrait sits on the brand red, framed in laurel, with a pull-quote in a light card at the base. The subject, not the logo, is the first thing anyone sees.
The template repeats deliberately: name, title, portrait, laurel, quote. Once, it reads as one story. As a running series, it reads as an award.

sections.heading: Making the Numbers Land
sections.label: Awareness Statistics
body: Where the award posters slow down for one person, the statistic posters are made to be read in under two seconds. "Only 27%" and "900 million" are set at a scale nothing else on the page competes with. The rest of the sentence is there to give that number its context, not its emphasis.
The 900 million poster pushes the idea further. The word "FINANCE" is redrawn as its own rising trend line, so the missing subject of the sentence is also the graphic that explains why it matters.

media.alt: Givfunds awareness poster reading 'Only 27% of adults in India are financially literate, that's 1 out of 4', with a woman holding a chalkboard drawn with a rising bar chart
media.caption: 1 in 4: the literal reading of a financial literacy statistic

media.alt: Givfunds awareness poster reading '900 million are left behind by a language they were never taught: FINANCE', with the F drawn as a rising red trend-line arrow
media.caption: The missing word doubles as the chart

cards.title: People, named and framed
cards.body: Exemplar Award posters give Givfunds' field partners a portrait worth sharing themselves, not just a client sharing about them.

cards.title: A statistic you don't scroll past
cards.body: National financial-literacy numbers redrawn to read in one glance, so the scale of the problem survives the scroll.
